notes: Main-split ABox revision of a stored fact (15 queries), migrated 2026-11-11. Cerf is the classic Internet-versus-Web confusion, so the edit is plausible and clearly false (the counterfactual has no hit in Dolma). Related near asks the old inventor ('Did Tim Berners-Lee invent the Web?', stored), with the single-inventor presupposition as a revision fact; Robert Cailliau is a collaborator, not a co-inventor, in standard sources. Its check was reworded: three models answered 'Team' to 'one person or a team?', which reads the question as about the Web's development, so it now asks whether the invention is credited to a single person. The earlier 'Did Vint Cerf invent the World Wide Web?' only reversed the direct question (review mark). Related far: the inventor's birth country (the United Kingdom to the United States), stated with the name. Derived: three compositions on the new value (TCP/IP, Google's evangelist title, birth year); there is no binding here, since the Web has no second name that is not a trivial variant. The indeterminate query keeps the W3C background split; its second question (the W3C founder's birth country) was dropped. 'Where was the Web invented?' was avoided: CERN would survive in both worlds. The conjunction's side fact is CERN near Geneva (true); the disjunction keeps 'Apple was founded by Bill Gates' (false). Evidence: counts reused from the earlier evidence pass (the infini-gram API returned 403 on 2026-11-11); new derived claims rest on Wikipedia full-text searches. Revised 2026-11-12 after review: related near is the plain inverse (Did Cerf invent the Web?, no to yes) with no uniqueness premise, since the single-inventor presupposition was a bridge, not a revision fact. Related (2026-11-14, two per record): near is the inverse of the edit (Did Cerf invent the Web?, no to yes); far is the inverse of the replaced fact (Did Berners-Lee invent the Web?, yes to no), with the single-credit revision fact as a check.
